title: knowledge(performance): Get behind a key-is-set check in and-condition wastes a DB call
summary: The boolean-operators-do-not-short-circuit article now covers Record.Get placed behind a key-is-set check in an and-condition. The pattern is not unsafe, but the Get is an unnecessary call when the guard means the key is not set.
key_points: New anti-pattern signal: Rec.Get(Key) behind Key <> 0 or Key <> '' when only a field value or default is returned
Best practice: exit early with a guard clause, then call Get
Get may be served from the server cache, so it is not always a database round-trip
GetEntryDescription samples added to the bad and good files, both using SetLoadFields(Description)
The existing article was extended instead of adding a new one
